I computed the July 2025 numbers from the official BTS on-time file. Firecrawl mangled the zip (it returned a corrupt 398 KB file), so I downloaded the file directly with `curl`.

**SFO departures, July 2025 (BTS Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance)**

| Carrier | Scheduled departures | Cancelled | Departures with delay data | Avg departure delay (min) | Share delayed >15 min | Share delayed ≥15 min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| United (UA) | 5,112 | 56 | 5,059 | **12.7** | **20.5%** | 21.3% |
| Alaska (AS) | 1,041 | 22 | 1,020 | **10.6** | **21.5%** | 22.1% |
| Delta (DL) | 1,233 | 9 | 1,224 | **14.0** | **23.6%** | 24.3% |
| Southwest (WN) | 704 | 5 | 700 | **21.9** | **37.9%** | 39.7% |

**Source**
- **File:** `On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_(1987_present)_2025_7.csv`.
- **Download:** `https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip`. It's the BTS TranStats "Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance" dataset. The zip's file timestamp is 2025-10-14.
- **Filter:** `Origin = SFO`, grouped by `Reporting_Airline`.
- **Average delay:** the mean of `DepDelay` across non-cancelled departures that have a value. Early departures count as negative minutes.
- **Share delayed:** the fraction of those same departures with `DepDelay` over 15 minutes. BTS's own "delayed" definition is 15 minutes or more, so I included that column too. Pick one for the slide and label it.

**Caveats**
- **Mainline vs. regional:** the data is by operating or reporting carrier.
  - SkyWest (OO) flies much of SFO's United, Delta and Alaska regional service, and it reports under its own code. Those flights are not in the figures above (OO alone had 2,951 SFO departures).
  - Alaska's regional partner Horizon (QX) did not appear in the file at all.
  - So these are mainline-only numbers. For example, they aren't "everything a United passenger boards at SFO."
- **Cancellations:** they're excluded from both measures. A cancellation rate would need to go on the slide separately.
- **Verification:** the file is from BTS's raw data release, and I didn't cross-check it against BTS's web "Airline On-Time Statistics" query tool.

Stripe shipped breaking changes in 2025 in only two API versions. Under Stripe's versioning model, only the first version of each named release can include breaking changes, and the other 2025 versions are additive.

| Date | API version | Release |
|---|---|---|
| Mar 31, 2025 | `2025-03-31.basil` | Basil, the first Basil version |
| Sep 30, 2025 | `2025-09-30.clover` | Clover, the first Clover version |

The other 2025 versions are `2025-01-27.acacia` and `2025-02-24.acacia` (Acacia), `2025-04-30`, `2025-05-28`, `2025-06-30`, `2025-07-30` and `2025-08-27.basil`, and `2025-10-29`, `2025-11-17` and `2025-12-15.clover`. Stripe's pages say these include only additive changes, and none carries the "Breaking changes" badge.

## 2025-03-31.basil

Stripe calls this "a significant number of breaking changes". The breakages below are my reading of the entry titles, not Stripe's labels.

**Billing**
- Discount coupons without a specified end time are no longer supported.
- The singular `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters are removed in favor of stackable discounts.
- Top-level price fields on Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items are replaced by new price modeling.
- Top-level tax properties on Invoices, Invoice Line Items and Credit Note Line Items are replaced by new tax modeling.
- Billing periods move to the subscription item level, and the subscription-level `current_period_start` and `current_period_end` are removed.
- The Upcoming Invoice API methods are replaced by the Create Preview Invoice API.
- Legacy usage-based billing is removed.
- Invoices can now take multiple (partial) payments.

**Payments**
- The manual capture method for Interac cards is removed.
- Partially capturing or canceling a payment no longer creates a Refund.
- Naver Pay payment method fields can't be modified after creation.
- The Vault and Forward API returns a 402 for upstream request timeouts.

**Checkout**
- Checkout Sessions for subscriptions now create the subscription only after payment completes, with new update semantics.
- Shipping details are removed from the Checkout Session.

**Cross-product**
- `total_count` can no longer be expanded on list methods.
- The `page` parameter is removed (listed for event destinations).

**Other**
- The Person object's political exposure property changes from a string to an enum.
- The Payment Element's default layout changes.
- Issuing webhooks now send a JSON Accept header.

## 2025-09-30.clover

**Billing**
- The `iterations` parameter is removed for subscription schedules.
- Promotion Codes now reference Coupons through a polymorphic `promotion` field.
- Discounts gain a `source` property, and the Discount `coupon` property is removed.
- Flexible billing mode is now the default for new subscriptions.
- Subscription schedule phase end dates now account for billing cycle anchor changes.

**Checkout and Elements**
- The `currency_conversion` field is removed from Checkout Sessions. Use `presentment_details` instead.
- `redirectToCheckout` is removed.
- `initCheckout` is now synchronous.
- Postal codes are no longer collected for card payments in Canada, the UK and Puerto Rico.
- Elements no longer lets you reuse Intent client secrets in certain states.
- Saved payment method defaults for Elements with Checkout Sessions change, so you no longer enable them in two places.
- Deprecated messaging and bank Elements are removed from Stripe.js.

**Payments and other**
- Decline codes change for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and the South Korean payment methods.
- Issuing Authorization risk levels now use standard values.
- Radar manual review enums gain new values.
- Risk requirement descriptions are more specific for sanctions, PEP and legal reviews.

## Caveats

- **Item labels:** Stripe's pages show the "Breaking changes" badge per version, not per entry. The lists above separate breaking changes from features by entry title, and some entries in them are additive. Check each entry's own page before relying on this.
- **Not read in full:** I read the release overview pages and the per-version entry lists, not the individual entry pages.
- **Account-specific:** Stripe says that signing in filters the changelog to the APIs your account uses.
- **Scope:** The Stripe docs show no breaking-change versions in 2025 other than these two. The 2026 Clover versions are outside your question.

Sources: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil and https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover. I saved copies in `.firecrawl/`.

In 2025 Stripe shipped breaking changes in two API versions, `2025-03-31.basil` and `2025-09-30.clover`. Every other 2025 version was additive only.

Stripe's model is that the first version of each named release carries the breaking changes, and later versions in that release are additive. I got this from Stripe's changelog pages for Acacia, Basil and Clover. The main changelog page was blocked by a captcha, so I used the per-release pages instead.

## `2025-03-31.basil` (March 31, 2025)

Stripe says this version "introduces a significant number of breaking changes." Changes to existing behavior:

- **Subscription periods:** Subscription-level `current_period_start` and `current_period_end` are removed. Billing periods now sit on each subscription item.
- **Invoice pricing and tax:** Top-level price fields on Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items are replaced by a new pricing model. Top-level tax properties on Invoices, Invoice Line Items and Credit Note Line Items are replaced by a new tax model.
- **Upcoming Invoice API:** The Upcoming Invoice methods are replaced by the Create Preview Invoice API.
- **Usage-based billing:** Legacy usage-based billing is removed.
- **Coupons:** Discount coupons without an end time are no longer supported. The singular `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters are removed in favor of stackable discounts.
- **List counts:** You can no longer expand `total_count` on lists.
- **Checkout Sessions for subscriptions:**
  - Creation of the subscription is postponed until the customer completes payment.
  - Lower latency and new update semantics.
  - Shipping details are removed from the Session, and shipping option updates are handled differently. I didn't read this part of the page in full.
- **Payments:**
  - The manual capture method is removed for Interac cards.
  - Partially capturing or canceling a payment no longer creates a Refund.
  - Naver Pay payment method fields can't be modified after creation.
  - The Vault and Forward API returns 402 for upstream timeouts.
- **Issuing webhooks:** The `Accept` header now specifies JSON for Issuing authorization webhooks.

The same version also added things like Satispay, Billie, NZ BECS, Naver Pay reuse, `ui_mode: custom` and billing meter webhooks.

The Basil versions that followed were additive only: April 30, May 28, June 30, July 30 and August 27, 2025. The August 27 version made flexible billing mode the default for subscriptions, but only in the public preview channel.

## `2025-09-30.clover` (September 30, 2025)

This is the first Clover version, so it carries the breaking changes.

- **Flexible billing mode default:** New subscriptions created on this version default to flexible billing mode. That changes behavior for prorations, trials and usage-based billing.
- **Subscription schedules:**
  - The `iterations` parameter is removed.
  - Phase end-date computation now accounts for billing cycle anchor changes.
- **Discounts and promotions:**
  - Promotion Codes now reference Coupons through a polymorphic `promotion` field.
  - Discounts gain a `source` property and lose the `coupon` property.
- **Checkout:**
  - The `currency_conversion` field is removed from Checkout Sessions. Adaptive pricing details move to `presentment_details`.
  - Postal codes are no longer collected automatically in Canada, the UK and Puerto Rico.
- **Stripe.js:**
  - `redirectToCheckout` is removed.
  - `initCheckout` is now synchronous.
  - Deprecated messaging and bank Elements are removed.
- **Elements:**
  - Client secrets for Intents in certain states can't be reused.
  - Saved payment method defaults change for Elements with Checkout Sessions.
- **Decline codes:** The decline codes change for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and South Korean payment methods.
- **Issuing:** Issuing Authorization risk levels now use standard values.
- **Connect:** There are new, more specific risk-requirement descriptions for sanctions, PEP and legal reviews.
- **Public preview only:** Platform-specific fields are removed from the Accounts v2 object. The Smart Disputes `recommended_evidence` field is restructured.

The Clover versions after that (October 29, November 17, December 15, 2025, then 2026 releases) were additive.

## Acacia in 2025

`2025-01-27.acacia` and `2025-02-24.acacia` were additive. Acacia's breaking changes came with `2024-09-30.acacia`, which was in 2024.

## Limits of this list

- The changelog tags a whole version as "Breaking changes" and doesn't mark each entry. I picked out the entries that remove, replace or change existing behavior. A few subtler ones, like some Checkout and Elements behavior changes, may be missing or misjudged.
- For the Basil list I read only part of the page. The Checkout section and anything after it, including the rest of the Checkout entries and any later sections, I didn't read. Clover I read in full.
- For pinning decisions, check each linked entry under `docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil/2025-03-31/…` and `docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover/2025-09-30/…`. Stripe's Dashboard also shows only the changes relevant to APIs your account uses.

Twenty states have a comprehensive consumer privacy law as of early 2026. That count comes from MultiState's February 2026 roundup and includes Florida, whose law is narrower than the others. The same source says no new comprehensive laws passed in 2025. I didn't check for laws enacted in the 2026 sessions, so verify against the [IAPP state tracker](https://iapp.org/resources/article/us-state-privacy-legislation-tracker) before relying on the count. Only the three January 2026 effective dates (Indiana, Kentucky, Rhode Island) are confirmed by that source. The rest are from my own knowledge.

| State | Law | Effective |
|---|---|---|
| California | California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), amended by the CPRA | Jan 1, 2020 (CPRA amendments Jan 1, 2023) |
| Virginia | Consumer Data Protection Act | Jan 1, 2023 |
| Colorado | Colorado Privacy Act | Jul 1, 2023 |
| Connecticut | Connecticut Data Privacy Act | Jul 1, 2023 |
| Utah | Consumer Privacy Act | Dec 31, 2023 |
| Texas | Data Privacy and Security Act | Jul 1, 2024 |
| Oregon | Oregon Consumer Privacy Act | Jul 1, 2024 |
| Florida | Digital Bill of Rights (narrow scope, mainly very large companies) | Jul 1, 2024 |
| Montana | Consumer Data Privacy Act | Oct 1, 2024 |
| Delaware | Personal Data Privacy Act | Jan 1, 2025 |
| Iowa | Consumer Data Protection Act | Jan 1, 2025 |
| Nebraska | Data Privacy Act | Jan 1, 2025 |
